claims.text: Urinalysis and urine culture for everyone.
claims.quote: Urinalysis and culture are always required.

claims.text: STI testing with a positive urinalysis, discharge or dysuria.
claims.quote: STI testing (all patients with positive urinalysis, discharge, or dysuria)

claims.text: Torsion strongly suspected: go straight to surgical exploration instead of testing.
claims.quote: If findings are highly suggestive of torsion, immediate surgical exploration is done in preference to testing.

claims.text: Equivocal findings: color Doppler ultrasound; a radionuclide scan if Doppler is unavailable, though it is less accurate.
claims.quote: If findings are equivocal and there is no clear alternate cause of acute scrotal pain, color Doppler ultrasonography is done. If Doppler ultrasonography is not available, radionuclide scanning may be used but is less sensitive and specific.

claims.text: Scrotal mass: ultrasound to confirm a testicular origin; then AFP, beta-hCG and LDH and a chest X-ray.
claims.quote: Scrotal ultrasonography can confirm testicular origin. If a testicular mass is confirmed, serum tumor markers (AFP, beta-HCG, and lactate dehydrogenase [LDH]) should be measured and a chest x-ray taken.
